subject: Run-rate & spike quota clarifications for Quantly pilot
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@quantly.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@quantly.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Run-rate & spike quota clarifications for Quantly pilot

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the pieces we promised to pull together: 

- What we heard: pilot will start with NLU/assistant traffic for internal analytics features. Primary concern: unpredictable spike windows during end-of-month reporting.
- Action items I have: pricing examples for the monthly run-rate and the 99th-percentile peak TPS that matter for SLOs; a simple mutual action plan showing timelines; ask for a short traffic sample CSV so engineering can validate batching and KV cache gains.

To get pricing into the right band, can you confirm the following by EOD tomorrow?
1) Expected steady-state monthly token usage (tokens/month) for months 1–3 — ballpark is fine (e.g., 10M, 30M, 60M).
2) Typical peak TPS during your heaviest 15-minute windows (99th) — absolute QPS or TPS is fine.
3) Target budget range you want to stay within (monthly $ or $/1M tokens target). If you have internal CP & burst allowances, mention those too.

Example pricing guidance (very rough stub to calibrate):
- $650–$850 per 1M tokens for high-priority low-latency gen at small pilots (if no commit).
- Reserved discounts apply for >50M/mo commitments — can push to $300–$450 per 1M depending on model mix and burst tolerance.

I’m looping in Marissa (SE) and Vanessa (sales) to scope any capacity bounding and to draft a short SOW once we see the traffic sample. Attached: a sample CSV template for traffic (Quantly_traffic_sample.csv) and an editable SOW stub we can iterate on.

Thanks — appreciate quick numbers so we can map to the right hosted tiers and a realistic $/1M.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com


From: Samir Patel <samir@quantly.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Run-rate & spike quota clarifications for Quantly pilot

Karthik —

Thanks for the recap and the template. Quick answers from our side after sync with Ops: 

1) Steady-state tokens/month (estimate): month 1 = 8M, month 2 = 22M, month 3 = 48M. These are conservative — we expect month 3 to be the first real production spike.
2) Peak 99th TPS: we typically see 350–420 TPS during the 15-minute end-of-month consolidation window. Occasional shorter bursts up to ~600 TPS for sub-5min windows.
3) Budget target: initial pilot budget is $6k–$9k/month. For production we can consider $35k–$60k/month depending on SLA. Our procurement team has asked for a dollar-per-1M target ideally under $400 for committed volumes.

I’ve attached a small traffic sample (columns: timestamp, avg_tokens_per_call, calls_per_minute) and a short note from our infra lead on burst tolerance.

Let me know if you want Priya (cc’d) to share more telemetry or a brief call with Marissa to validate inference latency assumptions.

Samir
Samir Patel | Head of Platform
Quantly
samir@quantly.ai

Attachment: Quantly_traffic_sample.csv (stub)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@quantly.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Run-rate & spike quota clarifications for Quantly pilot

Samir — great detail, thanks. I pulled the sample and ran a quick back-of-envelope. A few notes and a suggested priced example for the pilot: 

- With month-1 run-rate at ~8M tokens and month-3 at ~48M, we should plan for dynamic routing during the consolidation window (batching + prefix cache) to shave tail cost and maintain 95ms median latency.
- For 350–420 TPS sustained over 15 minutes, we recommend a small reserved pool with burst credit for the first 90 days while you confirm traffic shape. That reduces unit cost materially for baseline traffic.

Suggested pilot priced scenario (hosted API, mixed gen+embed workload):
A) No-commit pilot (on-demand): $700 / 1M tokens — estimated month-1 bill: $5.6k (8M)
B) Light reserved pilot (3-month commit of 30M total): effective $430 / 1M tokens after reserved discount — estimated month-1 bill: $3.44k (pro-rated) and smoother latency during spikes

Given your $6k–$9k pilot budget, option A fits comfortably but leaves little headroom for repeated 600 TPS microbursts. Option B aligns with your <$400 target only with higher commit. If you want to hit <$400 effective, we should be looking at ~60M+/month committed or a mix of model quantization and burst-tier routing.

Next steps I propose: 
- If you’re OK with a quick SE call, I can do a 30-minute latency/batching walkthrough today or tomorrow.
- Karthik / Vanessa, I’d suggest drafting a short 3-month reserved addendum and a fallback policy for burst overage. I’ll attach a sketch to the SOW draft.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Priya Rao <priya@quantly.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Run-rate & spike quota clarifications for Quantly pilot

Marissa / Karthik —

This looks good and helpful. We’d prefer Option B (light reserved pilot) if we can land around $420–$450 / 1M effective for the first 3 months — that gives us predictability while we validate.

Request: can you send an updated SOW that includes the 3-month reserved commit (30M total), the burst allowance for up to 750 TPS for 2-minute windows, and a one‑page rollback/fallback policy? If you can get a draft into our shared Drive link, I’ll route to procurement for a quick review.

I’m copying our procurement email: procurement@quantly.ai in case we need formal PO terms. We’ll aim to confirm by EOD Friday.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Rao | Head of Procurement
Quantly
priya@quantly.ai
